trips.name: Japan
trips.description: Honeymoon. 27 nights, Tokyo → Hakone → Fuji → Matsumoto → Takayama → Kanazawa → Kyoto → Osaka → Atami/Izu → Tokyo. Ground rules for this itinerary: one timed anchor per day, never two. Start time varies with what actually opens that day, but never later than 10:00. Nothing scheduled after 20:00. Travel days count as light days, not as free days to fill.

zones.name: Hakone
zones.summary: Onsen town in the mountains — hot springs, the Hakone loop and (weather permitting) Mt. Fuji views over Lake Ashi.

zones.name: Fujikawaguchiko
zones.summary: Lake Kawaguchi at the foot of Mt. Fuji — the classic postcard views.

zones.name: Matsumoto
zones.summary: Castle town in the Japanese Alps — one-night stop between Fuji and Takayama.

zones.name: Takayama
zones.summary: Beautifully preserved old town in the Hida mountains — morning markets and Hida beef.

zones.name: Kanazawa
zones.summary: Edo-period districts, one of Japan's top three gardens, and a great food market.

zones.name: Kyoto
zones.summary: Temples, gardens, geisha districts and old streets — four full days.

zones.name: Osaka
zones.summary: Japan's kitchen — neon, street food and day-trip base (Nara, Kobe, Himeji).

zones.name: Tokyo
zones.summary: Arrival city and grand finale — Shinjuku, Shibuya, Asakusa and everything in between.

zones.name: Atami / Izu
zones.summary: Seaside onsen town on the Izu peninsula — ocean-view hot springs, kaiseki dinners and a slow wind-down before the Tokyo finale.

places.name: Hakone Yutowa
places.description: Sep 25 – 27 · Hakone · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪1,920. Modern ryokan in Gora. Booking.com is offering an upgrade to a superior room WITH PRIVATE BATH, which implies the booked room may not have one — check and consider upgrading.

places.name: Mizno Hotel
places.description: Sep 27 – 28 · Fujikawaguchiko · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪810. One night before the Chureito sunrise. Upgrade offered to a superior room with balcony (lake/Fuji view). Confirm parking (you'll have the rental car) and ask about a very early checkout for the sunrise start.

places.name: Onyado Nono Matsumoto Natural Hot Spring
places.description: Sep 28 – 29 · Matsumoto · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪470. Natural hot spring baths, tatami-style, excellent value. Arrange takkyubin (luggage forwarding) here — bags go ahead to Takayama since you can't bring them into Kamikochi.

places.name: HOTEL WOOD TAKAYAMA
places.description: Sep 29 – Oct 1 · Takayama · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪935. You arrive here tired after the Kamikochi traverse. Confirm parking and whether dinner is included — you'll want it after that day.

places.name: The HOTEL SANRAKU KANAZAWA
places.description: Oct 1 – 3 · Kanazawa · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪1,664. Return the rental car THE DAY YOU ARRIVE (Oct 1), not the next day — Kanazawa is entirely walkable and parking costs money. Refuel before drop-off.

places.name: Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Shinmachi Bettei
places.name_ja: 三井ガーデンホテル京都新町別邸
places.description: Oct 3 – 7 · Kyoto · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪2,531. Machiya-style hotel on Shinmachi street, CENTRAL Kyoto — great for Nishiki, Gion and Pontocho, but a metro ride (not a 7-min walk) from teamLab Biovortex near the station.

places.name: Candeo Hotels Osaka Shinsaibashi
places.name_ja: カンデオホテルズ大阪心斎橋
places.description: Oct 7 – 10 · Osaka · Booking.com, confirmed, ₪2,056. Excellent Shinsaibashi location, steps from Dotonbori. Candeo's signature is a top-floor sky spa — check whether it's included. In-room washing machine, good for a laundry night.

places.name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
places.name_ja: ホテルグレイスリー新宿
places.description: Sep 19 – 25 & Oct 12 – 16 · Tokyo (Shinjuku) · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪3,233. The Godzilla-head hotel in Kabukicho — covers both the arrival leg and the final leg. Ask for a high floor away from the street; Kabukicho is loud until 3–4am.

places.name: Owakudani
places.description: Volcanic valley on the Hakone ropeway — sulfur vents and the famous black eggs.

places.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
places.description: Sculptures in the mountains, Picasso pavilion, and a foot bath.

places.name: Lake Kawaguchi
places.description: Lakeside walk and the Panoramic Ropeway; best Fuji reflections early morning.

places.name: Chureito Pagoda
places.description: THE Fuji photo spot — pagoda + Fuji in one frame. ~400 steps up; 20 min by train from Kawaguchiko.

places.name: Matsumoto Castle
places.description: One of Japan's most beautiful original castles — the black 'Crow Castle'. Evening light-up is lovely.

places.name: Sanmachi Suji old town
places.description: Preserved Edo-period streets — sake breweries, craft shops. Combine with the Miyagawa morning market by the river.

places.name: Kenroku-en Garden
places.description: One of Japan's three great gardens — go right at opening for near-empty paths. Kanazawa Castle is next door.

places.name: Higashi Chaya District
places.description: Geisha teahouse district — gold-leaf everything, including gold-leaf ice cream.

places.name: Omicho Market
places.description: Kanazawa's kitchen since 1721 — seafood breakfast (kaisendon) is the move.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
places.description: The thousand vermillion torii gates. Open 24h — sunrise or after 17:00 beats the crowds; full loop ~2h.

places.name: teamLab Biovortex Kyoto
places.name_ja: チームラボバイオヴォルテックス京都
places.description: Booked: Mon 6 Oct, 09:30. Japan's largest digital art museum — 10,000 m² over four floors, 50+ works, maze-like. Budget 4 hours, not 2, and go down to the basement on entry to hit the smaller rooms first. No café inside, so eat before. Free lockers, no bags over 50 cm. Sneakers (there's an athletics area), plain light clothing for photos, no short skirts because of the mirrored floors.
places.address: 21-5 Higashikujo Higashi-Iwamotocho, Minami-ku, Kyoto — 7 min on foot from the Hachijo East exit of Kyoto Station

places.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
places.description: Bamboo forest walk — combine with Tenryu-ji temple and the monkey park. Go before 08:30.

places.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
places.description: The gold-leaf pavilion over its mirror pond. 30–45 min visit; pairs well with Ryoan-ji rock garden nearby.

places.name: Nishiki Market
places.description: 'Kyoto's kitchen' — knives, pickles, matcha sweets, street snacks. No eating while walking.

places.name: Matcha stop in Gion
places.description: Placeholder pick — matcha parfait/tea house in Gion; expect queues after 11:00.

places.name: Universal Studios Japan
places.name_ja: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
places.description: Oct 8 — our full USJ day (Halloween season + the park's 25th anniversary). Tickets go on sale ~2 months ahead — expect Aug 8–14, 2026 — and you must buy the day they open: there are NO ticket booths at the park anymore (online only, via Klook). Get 2× Studio Pass + 2× Universal Express Pass Premium for Oct 8. The day-by-day plan is in the schedule; the complete guide we made is attached below.

places.name: Dotonbori at night
places.description: Neon canal walk, Glico sign photo — 5 minutes from the hotel.

places.name: Osaka Castle
places.description: The castle park is the highlight — nice at golden hour; museum inside is skippable if short on time.

places.name: Okonomiyaki & takoyaki crawl
places.description: Placeholder pick — okonomiyaki dinner around Dotonbori/Namba, takoyaki stands for dessert.

places.name: Senso-ji Temple
places.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, in Asakusa. Before 09:00 beats the crowds on Nakamise street.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing & Sky
places.description: The scramble crossing at dusk; Shibuya Sky observation deck needs advance tickets.

places.name: teamLab Planets
places.name_ja: チームラボプラネッツ
places.description: Immersive digital art in Toyosu. Book ~2 weeks ahead; you walk barefoot through water — wear shorts.

places.name: Ramen night in Shinjuku
places.description: Placeholder pick — Omoide Yokocho alleys are next to the hotel; ticket machines, cash only.

places.name: Don Quijote Kabukicho
places.description: Chaotic everything-store around the corner from the hotel — souvenirs, snacks, tax-free with passport.

places.name: Atami Sekaie
places.description: Oct 10 – 12 · Atami · Booking.com, confirmed, ₪6,768. Premium ocean-view ryokan — the pick for the Izu stop. A backup booking at Yuyado Ichibanchi (₪3,750, same dates) is still open — cancel it when you get a chance, both are free to cancel.

places.name: Kiunkaku
places.description: A 1919 seaside villa turned ryokan, now open to the public — gorgeous gardens and a coffee salon. A calm morning stop on the Izu day.

places.name: Atami Sun Beach & Ginza shotengai
places.name_ja: 熱海サンビーチ・熱海銀座
places.description: Palm-lined beach and the old shopping street right in town — easy on foot from the ryokan, good for a sunset wander in yukata.

places.name: MOA Museum of Art
places.description: Hilltop museum with sweeping sea views over Atami — one of three options for the Izu day (with the Jogasaki cliff walk and Shuzenji Onsen). Pick one.

places.name: Jogasaki Coastal Cliff Walk
places.description: Dramatic volcanic coastline on the Izukyu line, with a suspension bridge over the cliffs. One of three options for the Izu day (with MOA Museum and Shuzenji Onsen). Pick one.

places.name: Shuzenji Onsen
places.description: Bamboo forest walk and a 1,200-year-old temple in one of Izu's oldest onsen towns. One of three options for the Izu day (with MOA Museum and the Jogasaki cliff walk). Pick one.

places.name: Kinmedai & ise-ebi kaiseki
places.description: The local specialties — kinmedai (golden eye snapper) and ise-ebi spiny lobster, in season from October. Fresh Izu wasabi and sakura-ebi (cherry blossom shrimp) from Suruga Bay too. Best had as the ryokan's kaiseki dinner.

tips.body: Hakone Free Pass covers the whole loop (train, cable car, ropeway, pirate boat) and discounts many sights.
Use luggage forwarding (takkyubin) to send big bags ahead to a later hotel — travel the Fuji–Alps stretch light.
Fuji hides in clouds by late morning — plan viewpoints for early morning and check a Fuji visibility forecast.
Everything is walkable: station → Nakamachi street → castle in 20 minutes.
Hida beef is the local specialty — beef sushi at the market stalls, or a proper grill dinner.
The Kanazawa Loop Bus connects all the sights; day pass pays off with 3+ rides.
Buses get packed — prefer subway + walking; taxis are reasonable for 2 people on short hops.
Stand on the RIGHT on escalators in Osaka (opposite of Tokyo).
Get a Suica/Pasmo in Apple/Google Wallet for all trains, metro and convenience stores.
Trash cans are rare — carry a small bag for garbage.
Onsen etiquette: wash sitting down before entering the bath; towels stay out of the water.
Ask for a high floor on the Godzilla side; the head 'roars' on schedule from the 8F terrace.
Open 24h — sunrise or after 17:00 for photos without crowds.
Izu absorbs Pacific storms through October. If the forecast turns, stay north near Atami — Shimoda can get cut off.
Choose a room with a private open-air bath facing the sea if the budget allows — this is the trip's wind-down stretch.
Cancel the backup Yuyado Ichibanchi booking (Oct 10–12) when you get a chance — Atami Sekaie is the one you're keeping.

itinerary.title: Arrival day — not a sightseeing day
Land at Narita
itinerary.note: Scan your Visit Japan Web QR at the Joint Kiosk. Between immigration, bags and customs you'll be out around 20:30–21:00.

itinerary.title: Narita Express or Limousine Bus into the city
itinerary.note: 60–90 min. Buy the ticket before you head down to the platform.

itinerary.title: At the hotel
itinerary.note: Stop at a konbini for water, breakfast and something to snack on. Then sleep.

itinerary.title: Have the QR ready and your phone charged
itinerary.note: This is not a sightseeing day. Have the QR ready and your phone charged.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Head Spa 16:00 (booked) + birthday dinner · out by 9:00
Meiji Jingu and Yoyogi Park
itinerary.note: Calm mid-morning.

itinerary.title: Takeshita Street
itinerary.note: Long!Longer!!Longest!!! and I'm Donut?

itinerary.title: Lunch — Afuri Harajuku
itinerary.note: Yuzu-shio ramen.

itinerary.title: Omotesando → Cat Street: SNEAKERS
itinerary.note: Vintage shops, sneakers and quiet cafés on the walk down toward Shibuya.

itinerary.title: THE HEAD SPA SHIBUYA (90 min)
itinerary.note: Booked. Full scalp treatment, finishing with a wash and blow-dry — so you go to dinner looking good and feeling unwound.

itinerary.title: SUSHI KENSHIN — birthday dinner
itinerary.note: Tell the restaurant it's a birthday when you book.

itinerary.title: Sneakers: measure your foot in cm before you fly
itinerary.note: Japanese sizing is foot length. If you have wide feet, ask for Japanese Asics or Mizuno models in 2E or 4E width. Bring the socks you'll actually walk in. Backup if nothing fits: Alpen Tokyo, Shinjuku. And don't break in new shoes the next day — bring a comfortable pair from home and rotate the new ones in a few hours at a time.

itinerary.title: TSUKIJI
itinerary.note: Graze, don't fill up.

itinerary.title: Hama Rikyu, the garden next door
Back to the hotel. Long nap
itinerary.note: The 7:00 start is paid back here.

itinerary.title: MAGURO MART
itinerary.note: The tuna set, and the nakaochi you scrape yourself.

itinerary.title: Tsukiji is the outer market, not the wholesale one
itinerary.note: The auction moved to Toyosu in 2018. Before 10:00 or it isn't worth it. Graze in small bites: tamagoyaki, uni, a grilled scallop, strawberry daifuku. Bring cash and a small bag for rubbish — there are no bins.

itinerary.title: Sensoji
itinerary.note: Kaminarimon → Nakamise → main hall → Asakusa Shrine.

itinerary.title: Nishi-Sando
itinerary.note: Kagetsudo melonpan — before 14:00, it sells out.

itinerary.title: Suzukien
itinerary.note: Matcha gelato in 7 intensity levels.

itinerary.title: Sumida Park
itinerary.note: Skytree across the river.

itinerary.title: ANN FRAGRANCE Asakusa
itinerary.note: Custom perfume, ~50 min.

itinerary.title: Kappabashi
itinerary.note: Engraved knives, ceramics, chopsticks.

itinerary.title: Akihabara
itinerary.note: Yodobashi, Super Potato, gachapon.

itinerary.title: Kappabashi closes at 17:00
itinerary.note: Drop your purchases in a coin locker at Akihabara Station (¥400–700) and walk around unloaded. If you buy something heavy, several shops will send it to the hotel by takkyubin. No kimono in Tokyo — you do it once, in Kyoto on 5/10.

itinerary.title: Tourist discount card at the department store counter
itinerary.note: This first.

itinerary.title: Mikimoto, Itoya
itinerary.note: 12 floors of stationery.

itinerary.title: OMAKASE
itinerary.note: Lunch is far better value than dinner.

itinerary.title: Feiler flagship
itinerary.note: Japan-exclusive designs.

itinerary.title: Yurikamome from Shimbashi → Toyosu
itinerary.note: ~25 min.

itinerary.title: teamLab PLANETS
itinerary.note: Out around 20:00.

itinerary.title: Dinner in Toyosu on the way out
itinerary.note: Or something light back in Shinjuku.

itinerary.title: Leave Ginza empty-handed
itinerary.note: Ginza and Toyosu are directly connected by the Yurikamome — no need to go back to the hotel in between. You walk through water at teamLab and the lockers are free, but you don't want to carry bags all day; if you buy anything bulky, have it sent to the hotel. Clothes you can roll up to the knee, no long skirts (mirrored floors), shoes that come off easily.

itinerary.title: No anchor — deliberately light, Hakone tomorrow · out by 10:00
Isetan
itinerary.note: Discount card first.

itinerary.title: JINS
itinerary.note: Glasses, ready in ~30 min.

itinerary.title: Free afternoon
itinerary.note: Shinjuku Gyoen, or back to the hotel.

itinerary.title: Evening: pack without rushing
itinerary.note: Takkyubin to Hakone if you want to travel light.

itinerary.title: Don't buy consumables tax-free yet
itinerary.note: They get sealed and you can't open them until you leave Japan. That's 13/10.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Hakone Open-Air Museum · out by 10:00
Shinkansen Tokyo → Odawara, then on to Gora
itinerary.note: 35 min to Odawara, then the Hakone Tozan Line up. Check in at Hakone Yutowa.

itinerary.title: Afternoon: Hakone Open-Air Museum
itinerary.note: Sculptures and the Picasso gallery, about 2 hours. The best thing in Hakone.

itinerary.title: Anchor: the Hakone loop · out by 8:00
Morning: funicular Gora → Sounzan, ropeway to Owakudani
itinerary.note: The black egg.

itinerary.title: Midday: ropeway to Togendai, pirate ship across Lake Ashi to Motohakone
Afternoon: Hakone Shrine's floating torii
itinerary.note: Bus back to Gora.

itinerary.title: Fuji shows itself best in the morning
itinerary.note: Buy the Hakone Free Pass for the whole loop.

itinerary.title: Pick up the rental car at Odawara
Anchor: Oishi Park at sunset · out by 9:00
Down to Odawara and pick up the car

itinerary.title: Gotemba Premium Outlets
itinerary.note: Tourist coupon at the info desk — bring your passport.

itinerary.title: Drive to Kawaguchiko (1 h). Check in
Oishi Park

itinerary.title: Evening: houtou

itinerary.title: Anchor: Matsumoto Castle, last entry 16:30 · out by 7:00
CHUREITO
itinerary.note: ~400 steps, the Fuji-with-pagoda shot.

itinerary.title: Oshino Hakkai
itinerary.note: Eight snowmelt ponds, thatched roofs, spring-water tofu.

itinerary.title: Drive to Matsumoto
itinerary.note: 2–2:30 via the Chuo Expressway.

itinerary.title: MATSUMOTO CASTLE
itinerary.note: Last entry 16:30. Steep stairs — clean socks.

itinerary.title: Evening: Nawate-dori and Nakamachi
itinerary.note: Matsumoto soba, local sake.

itinerary.title: A 7:00 start is what makes both Chureito and Oshino fit
itinerary.note: Confirm the Matsumoto hotel has parking and what it costs.

itinerary.title: Route 158 → Abo Tunnel → AKANDANA car park
itinerary.note: ¥600. Direct shuttle in from there.

itinerary.title: KAMIKOCHI, 1,500 m
itinerary.note: Flat riverside walk: Taisho Pond (morning mist is the shot) → Kappa Bridge → Myojin Pond. 3–4 hours, no climbing.

itinerary.title: Shuttle back, collect the car, drive to Takayama
Evening: the ryokan
itinerary.note: Yukata, onsen, kaiseki dinner.

itinerary.title: Private cars are banned in Kamikochi
itinerary.note: Akandana rather than Sawando because it's on the Takayama side: you end the day an hour from the ryokan. Free foot onsen at the Hirayu terminal. There are no bins — you carry everything out. Eat at one of the Kamikochi lodges; there's nothing between stops.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Miyagawa Market, closes at 12:00 · out by 8:00
Miyagawa Market along the river
itinerary.note: Closes at 12:00.

itinerary.title: Takayama Jinya, the old town, a tasting at a sake brewery
Afternoon: Hida Folk Village (optional)
itinerary.note: Or the old town again, without rushing.

itinerary.title: Food: Hida beef
itinerary.note: Hida beef nigiri on a rice cracker. Grilled Hida beef in the evening.

itinerary.title: Worth buying: sarubobo dolls, sake, woodcraft
Return the rental car in Kanazawa — 15:30
SHIRAKAWA-GO
itinerary.note: 50 min from Takayama. Shiroyama viewpoint, Wada House, the rice paddies.

itinerary.title: Afternoon: Higashi Chaya in the late light
Refuel before handing it back
itinerary.note: Or they charge a punitive rate. Out-of-prefecture returns usually have to land inside business hours (until ~20:00) — leave margin. Check the one-way drop-off fee is included in what you were quoted.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Kenrokuen at opening · out by 8:00
Kenrokuen at opening
itinerary.note: One of Japan's three great gardens. The castle is next door.

itinerary.title: Omicho Market
itinerary.note: Kaisendon for lunch.

itinerary.title: Nagamachi samurai district
itinerary.note: 21st Century Museum next — the swimming pool illusion.

itinerary.title: Afternoon: back to Higashi Chaya
itinerary.note: Gold-leaf ice cream. A gold-leaf workshop if you fancy it.

itinerary.title: No anchor — arrival day, and it should stay that way · out by 9:00
Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa → Tsuruga, change to the Thunderbird → Kyoto
itinerary.note: ~2 h all in.

itinerary.title: Wander the neighbourhood with no plan
itinerary.note: Nishiki in passing, a coffee, the Kamo River.

itinerary.title: Pontocho by the river
itinerary.note: First dinner in Kyoto.

BAMBOO GROVE

itinerary.note: % Arabica.

Back to the centre

KIMONO
itinerary.note: The only one of the trip.

itinerary.title: Fushimi Inari
itinerary.note: Climb 20 minutes and the crowd disappears.

itinerary.title: Nishiki Market, then ARITSUGU
itinerary.note: Aritsugu, since 1560: buy a knife and they engrave your names in kanji.

itinerary.title: Kiyomizudera → Sanneizaka → Ninenzaka → Yasaka Pagoda → Gion Hanamikoji
itinerary.note: This is the sunset walk, and it's the whole point of the day.

itinerary.title: ENEN
itinerary.note: Grilled wagyu — order less than you think.

itinerary.title: Ask the kimono shop for an 18:00 return
itinerary.note: Or a next-morning return, which several shops offer. A 17:30 return means you miss the sunset, which is the whole point of the day.

itinerary.title: Head out
itinerary.note: Eat before — there's no café inside.

itinerary.title: teamLab BIOVORTEX
itinerary.note: Budget 4 hours, not 2. On entry, go down to the basement and hit the smaller rooms first.

itinerary.title: Free afternoon
itinerary.note: Philosopher's Path, Ginkaku-ji, a tea ceremony, or nothing.

itinerary.title: Kyoto farewell dinner
itinerary.note: Pontocho or Gion.

itinerary.title: This is not a two-hour visit
itinerary.note: 10,000 m² over four floors, 50+ works, maze-like: 3 hours is the sensible minimum and 4–5 if it's your first teamLab. 7 minutes on foot from the Hachijo East exit of Kyoto Station. Free lockers, no bags over 50 cm. Sneakers (there's an athletics area), plain light clothing for photos, no short skirts because of the mirrored floors.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Nara — the one travel day that's a real day · out by 8:00
Kintetsu Limited Express, Kyoto → Nara
itinerary.note: ~45 min.

itinerary.title: Luggage into the lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station
Nara Park
itinerary.note: Bow to the deer and they bow back.

itinerary.title: Todai-ji and the Great Buddha
itinerary.note: Year 728.

itinerary.title: Lunch in Naramachi
itinerary.note: Kasuga Taisha and its lantern paths if you still have legs.

itinerary.title: Collect the luggage. Kintetsu Nara → Osaka Namba

itinerary.title: Check in at Candeo Shinsaibashi
itinerary.note: Ask for a high floor.

itinerary.title: DOTONBORI at night
itinerary.note: The Glico sign, the canal, the giant crab.

itinerary.title: Late: Noguchi Taro Ramen Shinsaibashi
itinerary.note: 17:00–04:00, no sign on the door, 5 min from the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kyoto → Nara → Osaka is all one Kintetsu line
itinerary.note: No crossing the city, no changing operators. Namba drops you steps from the hotel. Luggage: simplest is the large lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station (~¥700). The alternative is takkyubin from the Kyoto hotel on the morning of the 6th — it reaches Osaka on the 7th — but then you need an overnight bag for the night of the 6th. There's a washing machine in the Osaka room; use it.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Umeda Sky at sunset · out by 9:00
Kuromon Market before midday
itinerary.note: Wagyu skewers, uni, scallops, fruit.

itinerary.title: Tennoji Park → Shinsekai

itinerary.title: Umeda Sky Building at sunset
itinerary.note: The open ring on the roof.

itinerary.title: Kushikatsu: never double-dip in the sauce

itinerary.title: No anchor, no start time — this is the trip's buffer
If you're tired, sleep in

itinerary.title: If you have energy

itinerary.title: If not
itinerary.note: Sumiyoshi Taisha, the Kaiyukan aquarium, or nothing.

itinerary.title: Check in at the ryokan. Yukata

itinerary.title: Kiunkaku
itinerary.note: 1919 villa, beautiful gardens, café room.

itinerary.title: Pick one
itinerary.note: MOA Museum (up the hill, sea views) / Jogasaki cliffs / Shuzenji Onsen and its bamboo forest.

itinerary.title: Back to the ryokan
itinerary.note: Long onsen. Second kaiseki. Nothing scheduled.

itinerary.title: Izu gets Pacific typhoons into October
itinerary.note: If the forecast turns, stay close to Atami — Shimoda can get cut off.

itinerary.title: No anchor — travel day · out by 10:00
Shinkansen Atami → Tokyo
itinerary.note: 50 min.

itinerary.title: Check in at the Gracery, Kabukicho
itinerary.note: Ask for a high floor away from the street — the area is loud until 3 or 4.

itinerary.title: Evening: Omoide Yokocho, yakitori in the alleys
itinerary.note: Or Ramen Street at Tokyo Station.

itinerary.title: Anchor: Shibuya Sky, 16:00 entry · out by 9:00
Coffee first
itinerary.note: Shops open 10:00–11:00.

itinerary.title: Bic Camera
itinerary.note: The ReFa. If you buy a hair dryer, insist on a 100–240V model — 100V ones burn out at home. Open the Bic Camera coupon on your phone before choosing.

itinerary.title: Don Quijote with the coupon
itinerary.note: donki.com/en → Service → Coupon. Live link, not a screenshot. Physical passport. Tax-free register.

itinerary.title: Drugstore
itinerary.note: Sunscreen, sheet masks, Melano CC, Salonpas.

itinerary.title: SHIBUYA SKY
itinerary.note: Booked entry is ~16:00 and mid-October sunset is around 17:05 — be up top before the light goes.

itinerary.title: Consumables get bought today, not earlier
itinerary.note: They're sealed and you can't open them until you leave Japan. Stack the discounts: tax-free (min. ¥5,000) + Bic Camera coupon (5–7%) + Donki coupon + department store tourist card (~5%). Always confirm before the register. If the 13th is grey, move Shibuya Sky to the 14th — you have the day free.

itinerary.title: No anchor — pick one, or none · out by 9:00
Yokohama
itinerary.note: Chinatown, Cup Noodle Museum, Red Brick Warehouse. 30 min away.

itinerary.title: Hidden Tokyo
itinerary.note: Yanaka and its pre-war lanes, vintage Shimokitazawa, Kagurazaka.

itinerary.title: Nothing
itinerary.note: It's day 26 of 27.

itinerary.title: This is the Shibuya Sky backup
itinerary.note: If the 13th was grey, today is the spare slot.

itinerary.title: Anchor: the farewell dinner · out by 10:00
Sleep in. Last konbini breakfast
itinerary.note: You'll miss them more than you expect.

itinerary.title: Final souvenirs and a serious snack haul for home
Pack
itinerary.note: Takkyubin can send the suitcases straight to the airport.

itinerary.title: Anchor: the airport run · out by 9:00. Don't waste the day at Narita
Check out, leave the bags at the hotel
Shinjuku Gyoen is 10 minutes away
itinerary.note: The best place in the city to do nothing.

itinerary.title: Last shopping in Shinjuku, a good final lunch
Collect the bags and go
itinerary.note: Limousine Bus direct from Shinjuku (85–120 min) or Narita Express (80 min).

itinerary.title: Be at the airport by 18:00
itinerary.note: It's a Friday afternoon: leave margin for traffic. Book the bus seat at the hotel desk.

shopping.name: Onitsuka Tiger Mexico 66
shopping.note: The classic sneakers — much cheaper here than at home. Try them on: Japanese sizing runs narrow.
shopping.shop: Onitsuka Tiger store or ABC Mart

shopping.name: Uniqlo HEATTECH base layers
shopping.note: The Japan-only range is wider and cheaper. Size up — an L at home is often XL/2XL here.
shopping.shop: Uniqlo (Ginza flagship is the big one)

shopping.name: Uniqlo UT collab tees
shopping.note: Japan-exclusive prints you cannot get at home. Good, light souvenirs.

shopping.name: Ichikami / Tsubaki shampoo + conditioner
shopping.note: The famous Japanese hair care. Cheapest at Donki or a drugstore, not the airport.
shopping.shop: Don Quijote or any Matsumoto Kiyoshi

shopping.name: Shiseido Fino hair mask
shopping.note: Tiny tub, cult status, costs a fraction of the export price.

shopping.name: Throat spray + hot-eye masks
shopping.note: The konbini throat spray the group swore by, and the Kao steam eye masks.

shopping.name: Regional Kit Kat flavours
shopping.note: Matcha in Kyoto, wasabi near Fuji — buy them where they are local.

shopping.name: Kitchen knife
shopping.note: Buy it in Kyoto or Osaka where the knife shops are, and get it wrapped for hold luggage.

shopping.name: Stationery haul (pens, notebooks)
shopping.note: Uni-ball, Pilot, Midori notebooks — a whole floor of them at Loft or Itoya.

shopping.name: Donki souvenir run
shopping.note: The one-stop shop for cheap gifts. Bring your passport for tax-free over ¥5,000.

reminders.title: Book Ann Fragrance Asakusa
reminders.body: For Tue 22 Sep, 13:30 — custom perfume, ~50 min.

reminders.title: Book the Kyoto kimono rental
reminders.body: For Mon 5 Oct. Ask for a plan with an 18:00 return (or next-morning return). A 17:30 return means you miss the sunset walk, which is the whole point of the day.

reminders.title: Start on the Ginza omakase
reminders.body: For Wed 23 Sep, 12:30 lunch. Tabelog / OMAKASE.in — some places open 2 months out. Backstop reminder on 23 Aug if this one does not land.

reminders.title: Book the farewell dinner — Hakkoku or Aramaki
reminders.body: For Thu 15 Oct. 60-day booking window opens today. If it turns out to be a monthly release, retry on 15 Sep.

reminders.title: Book SUSHI KENSHIN, Ebisu
reminders.body: For Sun 20 Sep — Luciana's birthday dinner. Say it's a birthday when you book.

reminders.title: Book MAGURO MART, Nakano
reminders.body: For Mon 21 Sep, 19:00. Reservations open exactly 1 month ahead, phone only, Japanese only — ask the hotel to call for you.

reminders.title: Ginza omakase — last call
reminders.body: For Wed 23 Sep, if it was not secured earlier.

reminders.title: Book the Shinkansen Tokyo → Odawara
reminders.body: For Fri 25 Sep, the move to Hakone.

reminders.title: Confirm the ryokan dinner at Hotel Wood Takayama
reminders.body: For 29 Sep – 1 Oct. You arrive off the Kamikochi traverse — you will want dinner waiting.

reminders.title: Book the Hokuriku Shinkansen + Thunderbird
reminders.body: For Sat 3 Oct, Kanazawa → Tsuruga → Kyoto. Both legs.

reminders.title: Book the Kintetsu Limited Express, Kyoto → Nara
reminders.body: For Wed 7 Oct, 08:30. Optional — reserved seats only.

reminders.title: Book SHIBUYA SKY, ~16:00 entry
reminders.body: For Tue 13 Oct. Entry opens ~4 weeks ahead. Mid-October sunset is around 17:05.

reminders.title: Book the Limousine Bus seat, Shinjuku → Narita
reminders.body: For Fri 16 Oct. Book it at the hotel desk. Be at the airport by 18:00 for the 20:40 flight — it is a Friday afternoon, so leave margin for traffic.
